questions.prompt: What bit count should be stored for zero?

choices.label: The maximum bit width of the input range.
choices.feedback: Zero has no set bits and supplies the starting value for later counts.

choices.label: Zero.

questions.prompt: How should the bit count for a positive number be obtained?

choices.label: Use the count for the number shifted right once, then add its lowest bit.
choices.feedback: Shifting right removes the lowest binary digit; adding that digit reconstructs the full set-bit count.

choices.label: Use only the previous number's count plus one.
choices.feedback: Shifting right removes the lowest binary digit; adding that digit reconstructs the full set-bit count.

questions.prompt: What should “dp” store after this step?

choices.label: Option A
choices.feedback: This stores “[0] * ((n * 1))” in “dp”. On this test, it raises IndexError: list assignment index out of range; the expected result is [0,1,1].

error.message: list assignment index out of range

choices.label: Option B
choices.feedback: This stores “[0] * ((n // 1))” in “dp”. On this test, it raises IndexError: list assignment index out of range; the expected result is [0,1,1].

error.message: list assignment index out of range

choices.label: Option C
choices.feedback: Set “dp” to a list of (“n” plus 1) copies of 0.

choices.label: Option D
choices.feedback: This stores “[0] * ((n - 1))” in “dp”. On this test, it raises IndexError: list assignment index out of range; the expected result is [0,1,1].

questions.prompt: Which values should “i” visit, and in what order?

choices.label: Option A
choices.feedback: This uses “for i in range(1, (n // 1)):” instead of “for i in range(1, n + 1):”. On this test, it returns [0,1,0]; the expected result is [0,1,1].

choices.label: Option B
choices.feedback: This uses “for i in range(1, (n - 1)):” instead of “for i in range(1, n + 1):”. On this test, it returns [0,0,0]; the expected result is [0,1,1].

choices.label: Option C
choices.feedback: Start “i” at 1, change it by 1 each time, and stop before “n” plus 1.

choices.label: Option D
choices.feedback: This uses “for i in range(1, (n * 1)):” instead of “for i in range(1, n + 1):”. On this test, it returns [0,1,0]; the expected result is [0,1,1].

questions.prompt: What should “dp[i]” store after this step?

choices.label: Option A
choices.feedback: This stores “dp[i >> 1] * (i & 1)” in “dp[i]”. On this test, it returns [0,0,0]; the expected result is [0,1,1].

choices.label: Option B
choices.feedback: This stores “dp[(i & 1)] + (i & 1)” in “dp[i]”. On this test, it returns [0,1,0]; the expected result is [0,1,1].

choices.label: Option C
choices.feedback: Set “dp[i]” to “dp[i >> 1]” plus (“i & 1”).

choices.label: Option D
choices.feedback: This stores “dp[i >> 1] - (i & 1)” in “dp[i]”. On this test, it returns [0,-1,-1]; the expected result is [0,1,1].

choices.label: Option A
choices.feedback: Return “dp” and stop this call.

choices.label: Option B
choices.feedback: This uses “return (dp)[:-1]” instead of “return dp”. On this test, it returns [0,1]; the expected result is [0,1,1].

choices.label: Option C
choices.feedback: This uses “return (dp)[::-1]” instead of “return dp”. On this test, it returns [1,1,0]; the expected result is [0,1,1].

choices.label: Option D
choices.feedback: This uses “return (dp)[1:]” instead of “return dp”. On this test, it returns [1,1]; the expected result is [0,1,1].
